items.caution_notes: Papers of Record waterproof packet; vessel registration; passports; passage clear-in/clear-out documents; medical documents; eyeglass scripts; permits/visas; insurance documents; wallets/ID for each person; handheld VHF (charged); USB battery pack (charged) with cables for phones and the satellite messenger; first aid kit; prescription meds; cash/credit cards; USB drive with the boat's documents + current boat data backup; sunscreen; survival kit; multitool.

items.name: Brief crew: no personal-device streaming underway, local media only
items.description: On a metered offshore link the biggest bandwidth risk is usually not the boat's own systems - it is crew/guest phones and tablets streaming video over the boat WiFi. A single streaming session can burn more data than everything else combined. Brief crew and guests before departure: entertainment underway comes from local media only, not internet streaming.

items.name: Arch / Hardtop - Mesh Net Storage Protocol
items.description: Ensure the no-see-um net is 100% dry and rinsed free of salt before stowing it away in a locker to prevent fabric mold or zipper corrosion.
items.caution_notes: The no-see-um netting must be bone dry and salt-rinsed before it goes in a locker - stowed damp it mildews black in a week and it does not wash out. Same rule for any canvas.

items.name: Autopilot - Quadrant Pin & Clevis Check
items.description: Crawl into the aft lazarette to visually inspect the heavy structural pin connecting the actuator rod to the rudder tiller arm/quadrant.
items.caution_notes: If the clutch ever welds shut you cannot hand-steer. Keep a dedicated 13/14 mm wrench zip-tied to the drive bracket to drop the clevis pin fast. 316 cotter pins and GRF-10 ball joints as spares.

items.name: Inflatable PFDs - Visual Indicator Check
items.description: Inspect the window slot on the inflator cap. The single or dual safety indicator dots must show solid GREEN.
items.caution_notes: Green in the inflator window before every offshore watch - one glance. Red or missing means the CO2 cylinder is loose or pierced, or the bobbin/hydrostatic has fired. Do not go on deck offshore in a vest showing red.

items.name: Propeller - Feathering & Gear Function Test
items.description: Underway, shift ahead / astern / neutral and confirm the blades open to the set pitch in gear and feather flat when the shaft stops.
items.caution_notes: A blade that will not feather drags roughly a knot and points to a dry or salt-locked hub - grease it before it seizes. Confirm equal bite ahead and astern; uneven means a pitch mismatch between blades.

items.name: Steering System - Backlash & Play Audit
items.description: Gently wiggle the wheel side-to-side with the brake off to feel for lag. Check the emergency tiller deck plate for alignment.
items.caution_notes: Brake off, wheel wiggled at the rim: more than a few degrees of dead motion before the rudder moves means a slack chain, worn cable or a loose key on the Mamba tube. Confirm the emergency-tiller deck plate is clear and its key is aboard - every trip.

items.name: Transmission - Oil Level Check
items.description: Engine level, before start: check the level on the combined filler-cap dipstick between the upper and lower marks.
items.caution_notes: A rising level means seawater is getting in past the output seal; a falling level means oil is leaking out onto the shaft. Either way, find it before the next passage.

items.name: Final hatch and port check
items.caution_notes: Personally check every hatch and port is closed and dogged before leaving (not 'someone did it').

items.name: Cockpit drains clear
items.caution_notes: Check the cockpit drains are free of debris and flowing; flush with a bucket if in doubt.

items.name: Documents current
items.caution_notes: Confirm insurance, USCG documentation, FCC licence, EPIRB registration and crew passports do not expire during the passage or the season. See the Papers & Registrations tasks.

items.name: Log the departure
items.caution_notes: Record time, position, barometer, heading and a backup GPS fix in the logbook.

items.name: Top off diesel and water; record the range
items.caution_notes: Fill diesel and water, and write the resulting range and fuel / water on board in the log.

items.name: Expiry audit - medical kit, light beacon, EPIRB, raft, ditch bag
items.caution_notes: Open the Expiry tab and clear anything due or overdue in the safety gear and first-aid kits.

items.name: Update the float plan
items.caution_notes: File or update the float plan with your shore contact before leaving.

items.name: Inspect all running and standing rigging
Ensure running rigging is in place and ready for use
Wash cockpit electronics
items.caution_notes: And other equipment covered in salt.

items.name: Put away passage-specific rigging and sailing gear
Inspect rigging & sails
items.caution_notes: Note any discrepancies.

items.name: Un-pickle watermaker membranes before first production run
items.caution_notes: Typical procedure (check your watermaker manual): reconnect the high-pressure hose pump-to-membranes, reinstall the pre-filters, lightly lubricate moving parts, then run the system depressurized on brine (overboard, not into the tank) for a minimum of 30 minutes to flush the pickling solution before switching the product-water hose over to the tank. Repeat the brine flush after every fresh pickling, not just a first-time reactivation.

items.name: Run the Layup Return Tool to bulk-defer schedule due dates
items.description: Back-in-service date -> due-date bookkeeping, not a physical task.

items.name: Safety gear spot-check - PFD/flare/extinguisher/liferaft dates
items.description: Especially important if the layup ran long.

items.name: Provisioning refresh before first passage
items.description: Review the Galley Meal Plan / merged food cart.

items.name: Reopen thru-hulls closed for an in-water absence, or set per yard splash sequence
items.caution_notes: Confirm bilge-pump discharge was never among the closed set.

items.name: Function-check the three deck fittings - fresh-water outlet, anchor wash, stern wash
items.description: Fresh-water outlet: operate the fitting and confirm the fresh-water pressure pump starts and water flows. Anchor wash: switch on at the Nav Station switch panel, push and twist the deck fitting, confirm the pump starts and water flows. Stern wash: switch on at the helm switch panel, same check. Look at each fitting and its hose connection for leaks.
items.caution_notes: Do the washdown checks only after the raw-water inlets feeding those pumps are reopened - the pumps must not run dry. Know which switch panel each washdown pump is on.

items.name: Run Engine Start steps (main engine + generator)
Complete watermaker startup / first production run
Keel-cooled refrigeration may restart only once confirmed waterborne
Prime AC seawater strainers before first run - Salon AC / Berth AC
Toilets back in service - confirm raw-water flush restored

checklists.name: Watch Handover Checklist
checklists.caution_notes: Set to recur every 6 hours to match a 6-hour watch - adjust the period to your own watch schedule.

items.name: Deck inspection by the captain
items.caution_notes: At the conclusion of his watch.

items.name: Brief the incoming watch - conditions & events
items.caution_notes: Current conditions; expected upcoming "events"; weather & vessel impacts; upcoming other-vessel contacts.

items.name: Brief the incoming watch - vessel condition
items.caution_notes: Anything broken; fuel/water used and left; current sail plan.

items.name: Systems checks
items.caution_notes: Main engine (inspect the engine room); monitoring dashboard review; power systems status; bilge status.

items.name: Alarms received
items.caution_notes: Note any alarms enunciated and outcome

items.name: Route Status
items.caution_notes:
1. Current Position
2. Distance from Course Centerline - if deviated plan for return
3. Distance/ time to next way point

items.name: Fishing Gear - Tether & Cleat Security Check
items.description: Inspect the high-tensile safety tethers and their attachment clips to guarantee they can withstand a 30-knot Wahoo strike at a 6-knot hull speed.
items.caution_notes: Check the rod safety tethers and clips - a hooked wahoo at trolling speed shock-loads a holder hard, and a rod over the side at 6 kn is gone. The tether is the backup to the holder, so it has to be rated too.

items.name: Fuel Polishing - Passage Fuel-State Log
items.description: Daily on passage (or at watch change): log which tank-set is feeding the engine, the gauge / sight levels port and starboard, and the RACOR restriction reading.
items.caution_notes: Running a tank-set dry sucks air into the high-pressure common-rail system and can mean a hard bleed and a stalled engine in a seaway. Switch sets with margin, not on the last inch. A restriction reading trending up over days = a slug of water or wax working toward the element.

checklists.name: Watermaker Startup / Shutdown Checklist
checklists.caution_notes: Typical sequence for a manual needle-valve watermaker - check pressures and flow against your unit's manual. The recurring flush / pickling / filter schedule is tracked as separate maintenance tasks, not repeated here.

items.name: Check pre-filter condition
items.caution_notes: Commonly 20-micron then 5-micron 10" spun-poly elements. Replace if they look contaminated.

items.name: Confirm the high-pressure needle valve is OPEN
items.caution_notes: Counter-clockwise, fully open. NEVER start the high-pressure pump with the valve closed - the sudden pressure change will shock the membrane.

items.name: Turn on the primer pump
items.caution_notes: Run for 2 minutes before starting the HP pump, to purge air from the system before it sees high pressure. Observe water flowing out the overboard line.

items.name: Start the high-pressure pump
items.caution_notes: Let it run about 15 seconds before touching the needle valve.

items.name: Bring the system up to pressure gradually
items.caution_notes: Over 1-2 minutes, increase operating pressure by slowly closing the needle valve. Watch pressure rise - the membrane starts producing fresh water at roughly 600 psi.

items.name: Set final operating pressure
items.caution_notes: Keep increasing pressure until the flow gauge reads the unit's rated output OR pressure reaches the maker's maximum (commonly around 900 psi), whichever comes first. Do not exceed the maximum - going higher makes more water but exceeds the normal operating limit.

items.name: Watch the TDS analyzer
items.caution_notes: Product water should stay under the maker's TDS limit (often 500-600 ppm). If it climbs and stays high, the membrane likely needs replacing (see the membrane task).

items.name: New/replaced membrane only - discard the first hour of product water
items.caution_notes: Do not drink water from a new membrane during its first hour of operation - it needs to flush out factory preservatives first.

items.name: ⚠️ Running limits - always in force
items.caution_notes: Never exceed the maker's maximum pressure (commonly around 900 psi). Never shut off the high-pressure pump under high pressure - close the needle valve first, or the sudden pressure change will shock the membrane. Never operate the membrane above 120°F / 45°C (e.g. don't let it sit in a hot engine compartment while running). Never run chlorinated water, laundry detergent, fabric softener, or any oil/lubricant/solvent through it - permanent membrane damage. Running the boat at high speed can introduce air bubbles into the membrane - true of all watermakers, not just this one.

items.name: Shutdown - open the pressure valve
items.caution_notes: Turn the needle/pressure valve counter-clockwise, all the way open, BEFORE turning anything off.

projects.name: Next Haul-Out
projects.description: Jobs to do the next time the boat comes out of the water. The anode and propeller jobs link to their recurring tasks in the maintenance library; add your own yard items.

tasks.name: Rigging - Stay Insulator Deep Inspection (mast out / rig slack)
tasks.description: If any stay carries insulators (e.g. an SSB backstay), then with the mast out or the rig fully slack pull the insulators apart far enough to inspect the insulator core itself for cracks - the routine in-water audit can only eyeball them under load, which can hide a hairline crack.
tasks.caution_notes: An insulator sits in the stay's structural load path: a cracked core drops the stay. Skip this if your rig has no insulators.

tasks.name: Thru Hulls - Replace legacy / suspect seacocks
tasks.description: Replace any seacocks that are original, corroded, stiff or of unknown age - hard-to-reach ones (e.g. cockpit scuppers) are the ones most often skipped when the rest are renewed. A haul-out job. Until then, keep exercising them (see Valve Actuation).

tasks.name: Deck Hardware - Teak grab rails: repair or replace (next haul-out)
tasks.description: Grab rails are handholds people put their weight on underway, so a rail that is cracked, rotted or loose at its fasteners is a safety problem, not just a looks problem - push and pull each one hard and stay off any that move. Work out which rails need repair and which need replacing, and check the deck under each base for water in the core when it comes off. Do it with the rest of the haul-out carpentry; the recurring Teak & Foredeck Handhold Check covers the day-to-day inspection until then.

tasks.name: Anode inspection/replacement - shaft, prop hub, strut, rudder stock
tasks.description: Haul-out is the easy access window instead of a dedicated dive.
